_comment: Brief 40 §B — THE VAULT RETENTION RULE, AS TRACKED INFRASTRUCTURE.
This file is the source of truth for the lock on blackbox-vault. It is applied with
`node scripts/provision-vault-lock.mjs` and asserted on every deploy by Brief 40 §C, which
reads the LIVE rule back and compares it against this file. Provisioning by hand in a
dashboard is how finding 7 happened: a retention claim with no artifact in the repository
SCOPE IS LOAD-BEARING, AND IT IS NARROW ON PURPOSE. The prefix is exactly the sealed-manifest
path (vault/<eventId>/<packageHash>.json). It must never be widened to the whole bucket and
must never be applied to blackbox-media, which holds capture chunks: a survivor who wants her
own recordings destroyed must be able to destroy them. The lock binds the OPERATOR, so the
record that an incident existed cannot be quietly removed; it does not bind the owner.
1096 days, not 1095: three calendar years contain at least one leap day, so 1095 can fall one
day short of the 36-month period the product claims. 1096 * 86400 = 94694400.
See scripts/vault-lock.mjs for §D — what this rule does and does not prevent.
